rule_en: 1st house: life, stature, colour, complexion, form and shape of the querent/native (in mundane charts the common people). Rules head and face; colour white; masculine; consignificators Aries and Saturn; Mercury has his joy here; called the Ascendant.
quote: It hath signification of the life of man, of the stature, colour, complexion, forme and shape of him that propounds the Question, or is borne
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.50 [PDF p.84]; consignificators/joy/colour on p.51

rule_en: 2nd house: estate, wealth or poverty, moveable goods, money lent, profit or loss; in lawsuits the querent's friends/assistants; in duels the querent's second. Neck; green; feminine, succedent ('Anaphora'); consignificators Jupiter and Taurus; Sun and Mars never well placed here (dispersion of substance).
quote: From this house is required judgment concerning the estate or fortune of him that asks the Question, of his Wealth or Poverty, of all moveable Goods, Money lent, of Profit or gaine, losse or damage
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.51 [PDF p.85]; continues p.52
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 3rd house: brethren, sisters, kindred, neighbours, short/inland journeys, frequent removing, letters, rumours, messengers. Shoulders, arms, hands, fingers; red and yellow; cadent; masculine; consignificators Gemini and Mars; joy of the Moon.
quote: Hath signification of Brethren, Sisters, Cozens or Kindred, Neighbours, small Journeys, or inland-Journeys, oft removing from one place to another, Epistles, Letters, Rumours, Messengers
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.52 [PDF p.86]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 4th house: fathers, lands, houses, tenements, inheritances, tillage, hidden treasure, the end of any matter; towns and castles besieged. Breast, lungs; red; feminine; North angle (Imum Coeli); consignificators Cancer and the Sun; father signified also by Sun by day, Saturn by night.
quote: Giveth Judgment of Fathers in general, and ever of his Father that enquires, or that is borne; of Lands, Houses, Tenements, Inheritances, Tillage of the earth, Treasures hidden, the determination or end of any thing
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.52 [PDF p.86]; continues p.53 (Sun by day, Saturn by night signify fathers)
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 5th house: children, ambassadors, a woman with child, banquets, ale-houses, taverns, plays, messengers; the father's wealth. Stomach, liver, heart, sides, back; masculine; succedent; consignificators Leo and Venus (Venus joys here); Mars or Saturn here show disobedient children.
quote: By this house we judge of Children, of Embassadours, of the state of a Woman with child, of Banquets, of Ale-houses, Tavernes, Playes
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.53 [PDF p.87]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 6th house: servants, small cattle, sickness (its quality, cause, curability, length), tenants, farmers, uncles (father's siblings). Lower belly and intestines; feminine, cadent, unfortunate (no aspect to the Ascendant); black; Mars rejoices here; consignificators Virgo and Mercury.
quote: It concerneth Men and Maid-servants, Galliflaves, Hogges, Sheep, Goats, Hares, Connies, all manner of lesser Cattle, and profit or losse got thereby; Sicknesse, its quality and cause
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.53 [PDF p.87]; continues p.54
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 7th house: marriage and the person inquired after, love questions, open enemies, the defendant, the opposing party in war, quarrels, lawsuits, the astrologer himself, thieves, wives and sweethearts, fugitives. Haunches to buttocks; dark black; masculine; West angle; consignificators Libra and the Moon; Saturn or Mars unfortunate here show ill in marriage.
quote: It giveth judgement of Marriage, and describes the person inquired after, whether it be Man or Woman, all manner of Love questions, our publique enemies
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.54 [PDF p.88]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: The consignificator glyph after Libra is a crescent (Moon) in the image.

rule_en: 8th house: estate of the dead, death and its quality, wills and legacies, dowry of the wife, the adversary's second, defendant's friends, fear and anguish of mind, heirs. Privy parts; green and black; consignificators Scorpio and Saturn; succedent, feminine.
quote: The Estate of Men deceased, Death, its quality and nature; the Wils, Legacies and Testaments of Men deceased; Dowry of the Wife, Portion of the Maid
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.54 [PDF p.88]; ends p.55
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 9th house: long voyages, religion and clergy, dreams, visions, foreign countries, books, learning, church livings, the wife's kindred. Fundament, hips, thighs; green and white; consignificators Sagittarius and Jupiter; the Sun rejoices here; masculine, cadent.
quote: By this House we give judgement of Voyages or long journies beyond Seas of Religious men, or Clergy of any kinde, whether Bishops or inferiour Ministers; Dreames, Visions, forraigne Countries, of Books, Learning
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.55 [PDF p.89]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 10th house: kings, princes, magistrates and officers in authority, mothers, honour, preferment, dignity, office, lawyers, the profession or trade. Knees and hams; red and white; feminine; Medium Coeli; consignificators Capricorn and Mars; Jupiter or the Sun here fortunate, Saturn or the Dragon's Tail usually deny honour.
quote: all sorts of Magistracy and Officers in Authority, Mothers, Honour, Preferment, Dignity, Office, Lawyers; the profession or Trade any one useth
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.55 [PDF p.89]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 11th house: friends and friendship, hope, trust, confidence, praise or dispraise, fidelity of friends; a king's favourites, counsellors, treasure. Legs to the ankles; saffron/yellow; consignificators Aquarius and the Sun; Jupiter especially rejoices here; succedent, masculine, 'in vertue' equivalent to the 7th or 4th.
quote: It doth naturally represent Friends and Friendship, Hope, Trust, Confidence, the Praise, or Dispraise of any one; the Fidelity or falsenesse of Friends
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.56 [PDF p.90]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 12th house: private enemies, witches, great cattle, sorrow, tribulation, imprisonment, all affliction, self-undoing, secret informers. Feet; green; consignificators Pisces and Venus; Saturn much joys here; cadent, feminine ('Cataphora').
quote: It hath signification of private Enemies, of Witches, great Cattle, as Horses, Oxen, Elephants, &c. Sorrow, Tribulation, Imprisonments, all manner of affliction, self-undoing
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.56 [PDF p.90]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Lilly presents these house meanings as Ptolemaic doctrine confirmed by his own practice and explicitly sets aside the Arabian subdivisions of the houses.
quote: This is the true Caracter of the severall Houses, according to the Ptolomeian Doctrine, and the experience my selfe have had for some yeers
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.56 [PDF p.90]

rule_en: A planet lying between the cusp of one house and the next is in the former house; yet if it is within five degrees of the cusp of any house, its virtue is assigned to the house whose cusp it is nearest.
quote: yet if he be within five degrees of the Cusp of any house, his vertue shall be assigned to that house to whose Cusp he is neerest
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IV 'How to erect a Figure of heaven by the Ephemeris and Table of Houses', p.33 [PDF p.67]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); djvu text line 12130
notes: Applied in western/houses.house_of_lilly to every house of the Lilly-school paragraphs. The same 5-degree reckoning is repeated for the 2nd (p.552) and 3rd (p.565) houses in nativities.

rule_en: Houses Capricorn (night) and Aquarius (day); exalted in Libra; fall in Aries; rejoices in Aquarius; rules the airy triplicity by day. Course 29 years 157 days; middle (mean) motion 2'01" per day; daily motion 3-6'.
quote: Capricorne ♑ his Night-house, Aquarius ♒ his Day-house; he is Exaltated in ♎, he receives his Fall in ♈
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VIII 'Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification', p.57 [PDF p.91]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Detriment is not stated in this chapter (see p.104 table, other session).

rule_en: Diurnal, cold and dry, melancholic, earthly, masculine; the greater infortune; author of solitariness.
quote: He is a Diurnall Planet, Cold and Dry (being farre removed from the heat of the Sun) and moyst Vapours, Melancholick, Earthly, Masculine, the greater Infortune, author of Solitarinesse, Malevolent
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VIII 'Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification', p.58 [PDF p.92]

rule_en: Well dignified: profound imagination, severe in acts, reserved in words, patient in labour, grave in dispute, studious of worldly goods, austere.
quote: Then he is profound in Imagination, in his Acts severe, in words reserved, in speaking and giving very spare, in labour patient, in arguing or disputing grave
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VIII 'Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification', p.58 [PDF p.92]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Ill dignified: envious, covetous, jealous, mistrustful, timorous, sordid, dissembling, sluggish, suspicious, stubborn, malicious, never contented.
quote: Then he is envious, covetous, jealous and mistrustfull, timorous, sordid, outwardly dissembling, sluggish, suspitious, stubborne, a contemner of women, a close lyar, malicious, murmuring, never contented, ever repining
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VIII 'Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification', p.58 [PDF p.92]

rule_en: Houses Sagittarius (day) and Pisces (night); course 12 years; middle motion 4'59".
quote: He hath two of the twelve Signs of the Zodiack for his houses, viz. ♐ his Day-house, and ♓ his Night-house
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.61 [PDF p.95]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Detriment Gemini and Virgo; exalted in Cancer; fall in Capricorn; rules the fiery triplicity by night.
quote: He receives Detriment in ♊ and ♍: He is Exalted in ♋, hath his Fall in ♑
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.62 [PDF p.96]

rule_en: Diurnal, masculine, temperately hot and moist, airy, sanguine; the greater fortune; author of temperance, modesty, sobriety, justice.
quote: He is a Diurnall, Masculine Planet, Temperately Hot and Moyst, Aiery, Sanguine, the greater Fortune, author of Temperance, Modesty, Sobriety, Justice
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.62 [PDF p.96]

rule_en: Well placed: magnanimous, faithful, bashful, honourably aspiring, a lover of fair dealing, wishing to benefit all, religious, affable, charitable, just, wise, prudent.
quote: Then is he Magnanimous, Faithfull, Bashfull, Aspiring in an honourable way at high matters, in all his actions a Lover of faire Dealing, desiring to benefit all men
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.62 [PDF p.96]

rule_en: Unfortunate: wastes his patrimony, lets everyone cozen him, hypocritically religious, obstinate in false tenets, ignorant, careless, dull, schismatical, abasing himself.
quote: When ♃ is unfortunate, then he wastes his Patrimony, suffers every one to cozen him, is Hypocritically Religious, Tenacious, and stiffe in maintaining false Tenents in Religion
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.63 [PDF p.97]

rule_en: Houses Aries (day) and Scorpio (night); exalted 28 Capricorn; 'depressed' (fall) 28 Cancer; detriment Libra and Taurus; rules the whole watery triplicity (day and night). Course 1 year 321 days; mean motion printed '31 degr. 27 min.' (i.e. 31'27" per day); retrograde 80 days.
quote: He hath ♈ for his Day-house, and ♏ for his Night-house; he is exalted in 28 degr. of ♑, and is depressed in 28 ♋, he receiveth detriment in ♎ and ♉
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. X 'Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations', p.65 [PDF p.99]

rule_en: Masculine, nocturnal, hot and dry, choleric and fiery; the lesser infortune; author of quarrels, strifes, contentions.
quote: He is a Masculine, Nocturnall Planet, in nature hot and dry, cholerick and fiery, the lesser Infortune, author of Quarrels, Strifes, Contentions
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. X 'Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations', p.66 [PDF p.100]

rule_en: Well dignified: invincible in war and courage, bold, confident, immovable, contentious, valiant, obeys no one, boasts of his acts, yet prudent in his own affairs.
quote: In feats of Warre and Courage invincible, scorning any should exceed him, subject to no Reason, Bold, Confident, Immoveable, Contentious, challenging all Honour to themselves
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. X 'Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations', p.66 [PDF p.100]

rule_en: Ill placed: prattler without modesty or honesty, lover of slaughter and quarrels, murder, thievery, sedition; highway thief, traitor, perjured, rash, inhumane, treacherous, violent.
quote: Then he is a Pratler without modesty or honesty, a lover of Slaughter and Quarrels, Murder, Theevery, a promoter of Sedition, Frayes and Commotions, an Highway-Theefe
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. X 'Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations', p.66 [PDF p.100]

rule_en: Only house Leo, detriment Aquarius; exalted 19 Aries, fall 19 Libra; rules the fiery triplicity by day; no terms (Lilly rejects giving him terms in the northern signs); always direct; mean motion 59'08".
quote: He hath onely the Signe of ♌ for his House, and ♒ for his House-Detriment. He is Exalted in the 19 degree of ♈, and receives his Fall in 19 ♎
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XI 'Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations', p.69 [PDF p.103]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Hot and dry but more temperate than Mars; masculine, diurnal; equivalent to a fortune when well dignified.
quote: He is naturally Hot, Dry, but more temperate then ♂; is a Masculine, Diurnall Planet, Equivalent, if well dignified to a Fortune
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XI 'Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations', p.70 [PDF p.104]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Well dignified: faithful, keeps promises, desire to rule, prudent, of incomparable judgment, majestic, industrious for honour, grave and few in words, secret, trusty, affable, magnificent.
quote: Very faithfull, keeping their Promises with all punctuality, a kind of itching desire to Rule and Sway where he comes: Prudent, and of incomparable Judgment; of great Majesty and Statelinesse
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XI 'Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations', p.70 [PDF p.104]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Ill dignified: arrogant, proud, disdainful, boasts of pedigree, purblind in judgment, restless, domineering, foolish, a spendthrift living on others' charity.
quote: Then the Solar man is Arrogant and Proud, disdaining all men, cracking of his Pedegree, he is Pur-blind in Sight and Judgment, restlesse, troublesome, domineering
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XI 'Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations', p.70 [PDF p.104]

rule_en: Houses Taurus and Libra; exalted 27 Pisces; detriment Aries and Scorpio; fall 27 Virgo; rules the earthy triplicity by day; retrograde about 42 days.
quote: Shee hath ♉ and ♎ for her houses, she is exalted in 27 ♓, she receiveth detriment in ♈ and ♏, and hath her fall in 27 ♍
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XII (Venus; chapter heading on p.72 not image-checked), p.73 [PDF p.107]

notes: Mean motion 59'08" is on p.72 per OCR (not image-checked).

rule_en: Feminine, temperately cold and moist, nocturnal; the lesser fortune; author of mirth and jollity.
quote: Shee is a Feminine Planet, temperately Cold and Moyst, Nocturnall, the lesser Fortune, author of Mirth and Jolity
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XII (Venus; chapter heading on p.72 not image-checked), p.73 [PDF p.107]

rule_en: Well placed: quiet, not given to law or quarrels, not vicious, pleasant, neat, loving mirth, musical, given to love-matters, cheerful, trusting, virtuous though often suspected of jealousy.
quote: Shee signifies a quiet man, not given to Law, Quarrel or Wrangling; not Vicious, Pleasant, Neat and Spruce, loving Mirth in his words and actions, cleanly in Apparel
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XII (Venus; chapter heading on p.72 not image-checked), p.73 [PDF p.107]

rule_en: Ill: riotous, expensive, wholly given to looseness and lewd company, careless of reputation, adulterous, fantastical, no faith or credit, spends in ale-houses, lazy, irreligious.
quote: Then he is Riotous, Expensive, wholly given to Loosnesse and Lewd companies of Women, nothing regarding his Reputation, coveting unlawful Beds, Incestuous, an Adulterer
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XII (Venus; chapter heading on p.72 not image-checked), p.74 [PDF p.108]

rule_en: Houses Gemini and Virgo; exalted 15 Virgo; detriment Sagittarius and Pisces; fall Pisces; rules the airy triplicity by night; never more than 27 deg from the Sun; mean motion 59'08", up to 1 deg 40' a day; stationary one day, retrograde 24 days.
quote: He hath ♊ and ♍ for his Houses, and is exalted in the 15 of ♍: he receives detriment in ♐ and ♓, his fall is in ♓
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIII 'Of Mercury, and his signification, nature and property', p.76 [PDF p.110]

rule_en: Neither masculine nor feminine of himself: takes the sex of the planet he is joined with; of his own nature cold and dry, melancholy; good with the good, evil with the evil; author of subtlety, tricks, perjury.
quote: of his owne nature he is cold and dry, and therefore Melancholly; with the good he is good, with the evill Planets ill
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIII 'Of Mercury, and his signification, nature and property', p.77 [PDF p.111]

rule_en: Well dignified: subtle and politic brain, excellent disputant or logician, eloquent, searcher of mysteries, learns without a teacher, desirous of travel, given to divination; no one exceeds him as a merchant.
quote: Being well dignified, he represents a man of a subtill and politick braine, intellect, and cogitation; an excellent disputant or Logician, arguing with learning and discretion
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIII 'Of Mercury, and his signification, nature and property', p.77 [PDF p.111]

rule_en: Ill placed/dignified: troublesome wit, frantic, tongue and pen against everyone, wastes estate in prating, great liar, boaster, busybody, tale-carrier, given to wicked arts; easily believes, constant in nothing.
quote: A troublesome wit, a kinde of Herenetick man, his tongue and Pen against every man, wholly bent to foole his estate and time in prating and trying nice conclusions to no purpose
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIII 'Of Mercury, and his signification, nature and property', p.77 [PDF p.111]

rule_en: House Cancer, detriment Capricorn; exalted 3 Taurus; fall 3 Scorpio; rules the earthy triplicity by night; no terms. Mean motion 13 deg 10' 36", never more than 15 deg 02' in 24 hours; never retrograde, but when slower than 13 deg 10' a day she is 'equivalent to a Retrograde Planet'.
quote: She hath the Signe ♋ for her house, and ♑ for her detriment; she is exalted in 3 ♉, and hath her fall in 3 grad. ♏
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIIII 'Of the Moon her properties and significations', p.80 [PDF p.114]

rule_en: Feminine, nocturnal, cold, moist and phlegmatic.
quote: She is a Feminine, Nocturnall Planet, Cold, Moyst and Flegmatique
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIIII 'Of the Moon her properties and significations', p.81 [PDF p.115]

rule_en: Well placed or dignified: composed manners, soft, tender, lover of honest sciences, delighter in novelties, apt to change habitation, unsteadfast, timorous, prodigal, easily frighted, loving peace; a mechanic learns many occupations.
quote: She signifieth one of composed Manners, a soft, tender creature, a Lover of al honest and ingenuous Sciences, a Searcher of, and Delighter in Novelties, naturally propense to flit and shift his Habitation, unstedfast
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIIII 'Of the Moon her properties and significations', p.81 [PDF p.115]

rule_en: Ill: a mere vagabond, idle, hating labour, drunkard, sot, without spirit or forecast, content to live beggarly, content in no condition of life.
quote: A meer Vagabond, idle Person, hating Labour, a Drunkard, a Sot, one of no Spirit or Forecast, delighting to live beggarly and carelesly, one content in no condition of Life
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIIII 'Of the Moon her properties and significations', p.81 [PDF p.115]

rule_en: Lilly's order of judging a nativity (Book III contents): things considerable before judgment (524); length of life (525); hyleg/aphaeta and the killing planet (527); Lord of the Geniture (531); complexion/temperament (532); manners (534) and their quality from the planets (539); understanding (543); stature and form (546-549); general fortune or misery (551); then house by house: 2nd riches (553-562), 3rd brethren (564-568), 4th parents (569-575), 6th infirmities and servants (576-586), 7th marriage (586-602), 5th children (603-605), 9th journeys and religion (606-613), 10th honour (615-623) and profession (624-633), 11th friends (634), 12th enemies, imprisonment, violent death (639-646); then directions (648 ff.), profections (715), revolutions (734), transits.
quote: Of the Lord of the Geniture, 531 Of the Complexion, temperament of the body, quality of Planets and Signes, 532 Manners of the Native, 534
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), The Contents (third Book), unpaginated front matter sig. (c 3) [PDF pp.55-56]

Note the 5th house is treated after the 7th; no separate 8th-house section was seen in the contents (death is treated under length of life/hyleg and violent death under the 12th).

rule_en: Before judging: rectify the nativity by accidents; take the fortitudes and debilities of all planets and the Part of Fortune; note houses, antiscia and contra-antiscia, and nearby fixed stars of 1st/2nd magnitude with small latitude.
quote: In the first place having rectified your Nativity by Accidents, which alone of all other wayes is most certaine; in the next place you must carefully take the fortitudes and debilities of all the Planets and ⊗
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CII 'Of things considerable before judgement be given upon a Nativity', p.524 [PDF p.558]

rule_en: Lord of the Geniture = the planet with most essential AND accidental dignities in the figure, best posited and most elevated; a near-equal planet participates. Lilly rejects Firmicus's rule; notes others use most essential dignities in Asc, MC, Sun, Moon and Part of Fortune.
quote: I am cleerly of this opinion, viz. That Planet who hath most essentiall and accidentall dignities in the Figure, and is posited best, and elevated most in the Scheame, that he ought to be Lord of the Geniture
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CV 'Of the Lord of the Geniture', p.531 [PDF p.565]; sentence ends p.532

rule_en: Temperament: collect testimonies of hot, moist, cold, dry from significators and signs; hot+moist sanguine, cold+moist phlegmatic, hot+dry choleric, cold+dry melancholic. Opposite qualities cancel; the Lord of Geniture and Horoscope counts threefold; the Moon in the ascendant counts twice.
quote: If Heat and Moysture overcome, the Native is of Sanguine Complexion: if Cold and Moysture, then he is Phlegmatick: if Heat and Drinesse, then cholerick: if Cold and Drinesse, then Melancholly
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, complexion/temperament chapter (begins p.532 per contents; heading not image-checked), p.534 [PDF p.568]

rule_en: Quality of the mind (manners): a planet in the ascending (or intercepted) sign is principal significator of manners, with any planet having dignity in its place; judge the significator and his dispositor (benefic and strong = laudable manners; malefic or afflicted and weak = corrupt). Mercury takes the nature of the planet he conjoins or in whose dignity he is; ☊ equals ♃, ☋ equals ♄ and ♂. Luminaries in the Horoscope matter little unless very strong.
quote: First, if any Planet do occupy the Sign ascending, or which is intercepted, he shall be principall Significator of Manners
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVII 'Of the Manners of the Native or Child', p.535 [PDF p.569]

rule_en: Second rule of manners: weigh the significator together with his dispositor.
quote: Secondly, consider that Planet who is the Significator, and his Dispositor; for if he be a benevolent Planet, or in aspect with such, and strong, he denotes laudable or compleat Manners, according to his nature
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVII, p.535 [PDF p.569]

rule_en: Worst manners come from the infortunes joined together, or with Mercury in the 7th, 8th or 9th houses.
quote: the worst manners are from the Infortunes, when joyned to one another, or with ☿ in the 7th, 8th or 9th houses
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, closing rule of the manners section, just before Chap. CIX, p.543 [PDF p.577]

rule_en: Wit/understanding: from Mercury and his configuration with the Moon; both well placed and in good aspect = excellent wit; square, opposition or no aspect = dull capacity. Mercury stronger than the Moon (in commanding signs) = reason masters passions.
quote: Significations of the Wit and Intellect are taken especially from ☿ and his configuration with the ☽, for he governes the rationall Soule and animall Spirits in the Braine
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CIX 'Of the Wit or Understanding of the Native', p.543 [PDF p.577]

rule_en: Significators of wealth: (1) the cusp of the 2nd (from 5 deg before it to 5 deg before the 3rd) and its lord; (2) lord of any sign intercepted in the 2nd; (3) the Part of Fortune and its lord, and Jupiter, general significator of wealth; (4) planets in the 2nd (nearer the cusp = more evident). Ptolemy's method: the dispositors of the Part of Fortune and their aspects.
quote: Thirdly, ⊗ and his Lord, and ♃, a generall Significator of Wealth
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'The second House of Riches, or the Goods of Fortune', p.552 [PDF p.586]

rule_en: Men's marriage: Venus and the Moon principally, then the 7th house and its lord, then planets in the 7th. Both Venus and Moon in barren signs (Gemini, Leo, Virgo) and cadent houses (6, 9, 12, and the 8th for its malignancy) argue a single life or aversion from marriage.
quote: First, you must understand that in the Marriages of Men ♀ and the ☽ are principally to be observed. Secondly, the seventh House and Lord thereof.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'The seventh House... Of Marriage: and first of Mens Marriages', p.587 [PDF p.621]; running head misprinted '787'

rule_en: Profession (magistery): significators Mars, Venus, Mercury (Mercury = wisdom and parts of mind, Mars = strength to endure, Venus = delight). Whichever is in the 10th, 1st or 7th in its own dignities, not combust or under beams, signifies the art; else one of the three that rules the MC sign and is in essential dignity (not peregrine or in fall); else the one partilly aspecting the Moon (strongest, best and most partile aspect, sinister before dexter); else the one aspecting the Moon within her orbs, unafflicted; else the one rising before the Sun. Failing the first two rules the native follows some ignoble trade.
quote: You are to consider ♂ ♀ and ☿; ☿ shewes the Wisdome and parts of the mind; ♂ the Strength of body to endure; ♀ the Delight
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLVIII 'Of the Magistery, Exercitation or Profession of the Native', p.625 [PDF p.659]; chapter begins p.624

rule_en: Three questions in judging profession: whether the native shall have any profession at all; what kind; and what fortune and fame he shall have in it.
quote: Three things are wont to be considered in this Judgement.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLVIII, p.624 [PDF p.658]; items continue p.625

rule_en: Honour/dignity (10th house) is judged from the two luminaries, the Sun, the Moon, the Mid-heaven, the ascendant and fixed stars (per contents pp.615-623).
quote: Rules from the two Laminaries, 617
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), The Contents (third Book), unpaginated front matter sig. (c 3) [PDF p.56]

rule_en: Annual profection: one whole sign (30 deg) per solar year, counted from the radical ascendant degree in order of signs (e.g. Asc 6 Gemini: year 1 from 6 Gemini to 6 Cancer; year 2 from 6 Cancer to 6 Leo...); cycle repeats every 12 years. Every house cusp keeps its radical degree and minute, only the sign advances.
quote: Profection is threefold; one Annuall, wherein we give thirty degrees, or one whole Signe to a solar yeer
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVI 'Of annuall Profections, and by what meanes to find out the Profectionall Signe of every yeer', p.715 [PDF p.749]

rule_en: The profectional year begins at the solar return (the Sun's return to its radical degree and minute), not on the calendar birthday.
quote: you must begin the yeer of Profection, at what time the ☉ returnes to the degree and minute he was in at the Radix, and for this cause it is called a Solar yeer
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVI, p.716 [PDF p.750]

rule_en: Monthly profection: one sign per profectional month, the year divided into 13 equal parts; diurnal profection: one sign per 2 days 3 h 54 min. Lilly uses only annual profections, calling the others over-scrupulous.
quote: I will onely proceed to annuall Profections, holding this opinion, That if one should follow the nicenesse of the Ancients in every particular, it were impossible to judge one Nativity exactly in halfe a yeers time.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVI, p.716 [PDF p.750]

rule_en: Judging a profection figure: examine the profected ascending sign's radical house and condition (angle/succedent/cadent, its lord, exaltation and triplicity rulers, planets, Part of Fortune or antiscia there, aspects, fixed stars, light/dark degrees). If the profected sign is free from affliction and its lord is direct, strong and well placed both in the radix and in the annual solar-return figure, the year will be successful.
quote: In the first place consider the Sign ascending in the Profection, what place it had in the Radix
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVIII 'How to judge upon a Figure of Profections', p.726 [PDF p.760]

rule_en: For yearly health consider five things: the sign of the profection; the terms the Horoscope (directed) comes to; the terms the Aphaeta (hyleg) is in; the position of the Moon; the ascendant of the annual revolution of the Sun.
quote: The Signe of the Profection. 2. The termes unto which the Horoscope comes. 3. The termes in which the Aptæta is at that time. 4. The position of the ☽. 5. The Ascendant
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVIII, p.726 [PDF p.760]

notes: 'Aptæta' as printed (misprint for Aphæta); item 5 continues 'of the Figure in the Annuall resolution of the ☉'.

rule_en: Lord of the year = ruler of the sign ascending in the profection. When the profected ascendant spans two signs within the year, each ruler governs for the part of the year proportional to the degrees (Lilly's worked example converts 23 deg 23' to 284 days). Lord of the year strong in the radix but weak in the revolution = weak endeavours that year; afflicted in radix but strong in the revolution = moderate good.
quote: You must next in order consider the Lord of the yeer, who is ever that Planet that is Lord of the Signe ascending in the Profection
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVIII, p.727 [PDF p.761]

rule_en: Revolution (solar return): the figure cast for the Sun's exact return to its radical degree and minute; radical Sun must be computed precisely since 1 minute of solar motion gives about 24 minutes of time. Method: Sun's longitude at noon on the return day, interpolate by its daily motion to the exact time (Maginus and Argoli give easier methods). Example: revolution for the native's 31st year by Maginus's method.
quote: a Revolution or annuall Conversion is no other then the returne of the ☉ to that very poynt wherein at the Radix of any Nativity or matter he was
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXXII 'Of Revolutions', p.734 [PDF p.768]

rule_en: Precision of the radical Sun governs the solar-return time: one minute of solar motion error gives 24 minutes of clock error.
quote: for the mistake of one minute in the ☉ his motion, will beget 24. minutes errour in time
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXXII, p.734 [PDF p.768]

rule_en: Aries: masculine, diurnal, movable, cardinal, equinoctial; fiery, hot and dry, choleric, bestial, luxurious, intemperate and violent; diurnal house of Mars; fiery triplicity; East. Person: dry body, not tall, lean or spare but strong-limbed, long visage, black eyebrows, long neck, thick shoulders, dusky brown or swarthy.
quote: Is a Masculine, Diurnall Signe, movable, Cardinall, Equinoctiall; in nature fiery, hot and dry, cholericke, bestial, luxurious, intemperate and violent: the diurnall house of ♂, of the Fiery Triplicity, and of the East.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XVI 'The Nature, Place, Countries, generall Description, and Diseases signified by the twelve signes', p.93 [PDF p.127]; description continues on PDF p.128 (printed '95')

rule_en: Taurus: earthy, cold, dry, melancholy, feminine, nocturnal, fixed, domestical or bestial; earthy triplicity; South; night house of Venus. Person: short but full, strong, well-set stature, broad forehead, great eyes, big face, large shoulders, great mouth, thick lips, black rugged hair.
quote: Is an Earthly, Cold, Dry, Melancholy, Feminine, Nocturnal, Fixed, Domestical or Bestial Signe, of the Earthly Triplicity, and South, the Night-house of Venus.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XVI 'The Nature, Place, Countries, generall Description, and Diseases signified by the twelve signes', p.95 (as printed; true p.94) [PDF p.128]

rule_en: Gemini: airy, hot, moist, sanguine, diurnal, common or double-bodied human sign; diurnal house of Mercury; airy triplicity; Western; masculine. Person: upright, tall, straight body, sanguine but obscure complexion, long arms, dark hair almost black, strong active body, piercing hazel eye, excellent understanding.
quote: It's an aerial, hot, moyst, sanguine, Diurnal, common or double-bodied humain Signe; the diurnall house of ☿: of the aery triplicity, Westerne, Masculine.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XVI 'The Nature, Place, Countries, generall Description, and Diseases signified by the twelve signes', p.95 (as printed; true p.94) [PDF p.128]; description continues on PDF p.129 (printed '94')

rule_en: Cancer: only house of the Moon; first sign of the watery or northern triplicity; watery, cold, moist, phlegmatic, feminine, nocturnal, movable, solstice sign; mute and slow of voice; fruitful; Northern. Person: low, small stature, upper parts bigger, round visage, sickly pale whitish complexion, sad brown hair, little eyes; if a woman, prone to many children.
quote: Is the onely house of the Moon, and is the first Signe of the Watry or Northerne Triplicity, is Watry, Cold, Moyst, Flegmatick, Feminine, Nocturnal, Moveable, a Solstice Signe, mute and slow of Voyce, Fruitful, Northerne.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XVI 'The Nature, Place, Countries, generall Description, and Diseases signified by the twelve signes', p.94 (as printed; true p.95) [PDF p.129]

rule_en: Leo: only house of the Sun; fiery, hot, dry, choleric, diurnal, commanding, bestial, barren; of the East and fiery triplicity; masculine. Person: great round head, big staring eyes, quick-sighted, full large body, middle stature, broad shoulders, narrow sides, yellow or dark flaxen curling hair, fierce countenance but ruddy, high sanguine complexion, strong, valiant, active.
quote: Is the onely house of the Sun, by nature, Fiery, Hot, Dry, Cholerick, Diurnal, Commanding, Bestial, Barren, of the East, and Fiery Triplicity, Masculine.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XVI 'The Nature, Place, Countries, generall Description, and Diseases signified by the twelve signes', p.94 (as printed; true p.95) [PDF p.129]; description ends p.96

rule_en: Virgo: earthy, cold, melancholy, barren, feminine, nocturnal, Southern; house and exaltation of Mercury; earthy triplicity. Person: slender body of mean height, decently composed, ruddy brown complexion, black hair, well-favoured but no beauty, small shrill voice, witty, discreet, judicious, well-spoken, studious, given to history.
quote: It's an earthly, cold, melancholly, barren, feminine, nocturnall, Southerne Signe; the house and exaltation of ☿, of the earthly triplicity.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XVI 'The Nature, Place, Countries, generall Description, and Diseases signified by the twelve signes', p.96 [PDF p.130]

rule_en: Libra: airy, hot and moist, sanguine, masculine, movable, equinoctial, cardinal, human, diurnal; airy triplicity; Western; chief house of Venus. Person: well-framed straight tall body, more subtle than gross, round lovely beautiful visage, pure sanguine colour, pimples or high colour in age, yellowish smooth long hair.
quote: Is a Signe aeriall, hot and moyst, Sanguine, Masculine, Moveable, Equinoctiall, Cardinall, Humaine, Diurnall, of the Ærial Triplicity, and Western, the chiefe House of ♀.

rule_en: Scorpio: cold, watery, nocturnal, phlegmatic, feminine; watery triplicity; fixed; North; house and joy of Mars; usually represents subtle, deceitful men. Person: corpulent, strong, able body, broad or square face, dusky muddy complexion, sad dark crisping hair, hairy body, somewhat bow-legged, short-necked, squat.
quote: Is a cold, watry, nocturnal, flegmatick, feminine Signe, of the watry Triplicity, fixed and North, the house and joy of Mars, feminine; usually it doth represent subtill, deceitfull men.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XVI 'The Nature, Place, Countries, generall Description, and Diseases signified by the twelve signes', p.97 [PDF p.131]

rule_en: Sagittarius: fiery triplicity; East; fiery, hot, dry, masculine, choleric, diurnal, common, bicorporeal or double-bodied; house and joy of Jupiter. Person: well-favoured countenance, somewhat long but full and ruddy visage, almost sunburnt, light chestnut hair, stature somewhat above middle size, strong able body.
quote: Is of the fiery triplicity, East, in nature fiery, hot, dry, Masculine, Cholericke, Diurnall, Common, bycorporall or double bodied, the House and joy of ♃.

rule_en: Capricorn: house of Saturn; nocturnal, cold, dry, melancholy, earthy, feminine, solsticial, cardinal, movable, domestical, four-footed, Southern; exaltation of Mars. Person: usually dry bodies, not tall, long lean slender visage, thin beard, black hair, narrow chin, long small neck, narrow breast.
quote: It's the House of Saturn, and is Nocturnal, Cold, Dry, Melancholly, Earthly, Feminine, Solsticiall, Cardinall, Moveable, Domesticall, Fourfooted, Southerne; the exaltation of ♂.

rule_en: Aquarius: airy, hot and moist; airy triplicity; diurnal, sanguine, fixed, rational, human, masculine; principal house of Saturn, where he most rejoices; Western. Person: squat thick corporature or strong well-composed body, not tall, long visage, sanguine complexion; with Saturn in ♑ or ♒ black hair and distorted teeth, otherwise clear fair complexion and sandy or flaxen hair.
quote: Is an aierial, hot and moyst Signe, of the aiery Triplicity, diurnal, sanguine, fixed, rational, humane, masculine, the principall house of ♄, and house wherein he most rejoyceth; Westerne.

quote: Is of the Watry Triplicity, Northern, cold Signe, moyst, Flegmatick, feminine, nocturnal, the house of Jupiter, and exaltation of Venus, a Bycorporeal, common or double-bodied Signe, an idle, effeminate, sickly Signe

rule_en: Four temperaments: sanguine (temperately hot and moist), phlegmatic (moist and cold), choleric (hot and dry), melancholic (cold and dry). They are known from the qualities of the significators of temperament, collecting testimonies of hot, cold, moist, dry.
quote: Sanguine, which is temperately hot and moyst; Phlegmatick, which is moyst and cold; Cholerick, which is hot and dry; Melancholick, which is cold and dry.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVI 'Of the Complexion or Temperament of the Body, quality of the Planets and Signes', p.532 [PDF p.566]

rule_en: Significators of the complexion, as printed: (1) the sign ascending and its lord; (2) the planet(s) in the ascendant, or ☊ or ☋, or planets partilly aspecting the ascendant; (3) the Moon and the planet(s) beholding her within the moiety of their orbs; (4) the quarter of the year or sign the Sun is in; (5) the Lord of the Geniture. Examine the quality of each significator and of the sign it is in.
quote: First, The Signe ascending, and Lord thereof. Secondly, The Planet or Planets placed in the ascendant, or the ☊ or ☋ or the Planets partilly aspecting the ascendant.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVI 'Of the Complexion or Temperament of the Body, quality of the Planets and Signes', p.533 [PDF p.567]

rule_en: Significators 3-5 of the complexion: the Moon and planets aspecting her within half their orbs; the quarter of the year (sign of the Sun); the Lord of the Geniture.

rule_en: Quality of the planets for temperament: ♄ oriental cold and moist, occidental dry; ♃ oriental hot and moist, occidental moist; ♂ oriental hot and dry, occidental dry; ♀ oriental hot and moist, occidental moist; ☿ oriental hot, occidental dry. ☊ counts as ♃, ☋ as ♄ and ♂.

rule_en: When the Moon is directed to the terms or aspect of a planet the native shows that planet's manners: to Venus cheerful; to Jupiter discreet, modest, religious; to Mars angry, choleric, quarrelsome; to Saturn grave, melancholy, sullen, fearful, laborious.
quote: if the ☽ comes to the Terms or aspect of ♀, the Native is Cheerfull; to the Termes or aspect of ♃, Discreet, Modest, Religious; to the Termes of ♂, Angry, Cholerick, Quarrelsome

rule_en: Fallback order for the significator of manners: no planet in the ascendant, then the planet joined to the Moon or Mercury; if none, the Lord of the ascendant (judged with his dispositor's aspect); if no aspect, the planet partilly aspecting Moon and Mercury; if none, the planet with most essential dignities in the places of Mercury and the Moon.
quote: No Planet in the ascendant, or joyned to Mercury or Luna, then take the Lord of the ascendant, according to his nature, be it good or ill, and so judge of the manners
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVII 'Of the Manners of the Native or Child', p.536 [PDF p.570]

rule_en: Manners by temperament: sanguine cheerful, liberal, faithful, affable; choleric angry, quarrelsome, revengeful, ambitious, rash; melancholic slow in resolution, fraudulent, secret, covetous, suspicious; phlegmatic cowardly, mutable, dull, sluggish.
quote: Phlegmatick, are very cowards, uxorious people, mutable, not capable of keeping secrets, dull fellowes and sluggards in performing any businesse.

rule_en: Generalised sign rules for the significator of manners (from the Ancients): ♈ witty, ingenious; ♉ laborious; ♊ witty, deceitful, lover of arts; ♋ unconstant; ♌ grave but a little cruel; ♍ loves learning, covetous; ♎ inconstant, crafty; ♏ impudent but of good understanding; ♐ valiant; ♑ lecherous; ♒ humane, affable; ♓ stammering, fraudulent, hypocrite.
quote: The Ancients have therefore delivered, That when the Significator of Manners is in ♈, he incites the Native to be witty and ingenious.

rule_en: No separate Sun/Moon manner portraits in Chap. CVIII. The Moon with the principal significator, increasing in light, makes the manners appear sooner; combust or under beams, less manifest; at greatest latitude, varied manners. The Sun with a strong significator adds gravity with pleasantness; weak, less graceful. The dispositors of the luminaries matter more than the luminaries themselves.
quote: Yet it is generally observed, that it is more materiall to consider the Dispositors of the Luminaries, then themselves
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVIII 'The quality of Manners, which may in kind be discerned from every Planet', p.542 [PDF p.576]

rule_en: Mixtures: ♄ significator with ♃ joined by body or aspect, ♃ qualifies ♄'s ill nature (prudent, wise, quiet, of great counsel), when ♃ is fairly strong; ♂ with ♄ undertakes but seldom concludes, a bragger, turbulent, seditious.
quote: If ♄ be Significator of Manners and ♃ be joyned with him by body or aspect, ♃ then qualifies the ill nature of ♄
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVIII 'The quality of Manners, which may in kind be discerned from every Planet', p.542 [PDF p.576]

rule_en: Women's marriage: significators are the Sun and Mars first, then the 7th house and its lord, then planets in the 7th. Judge as for men, putting the Sun in place of the Moon and Mars in place of Venus; consider barren or prolific, double-bodied or fruitful signs, fortunes or infortunes, strong or weak.
quote: First, their Significators are ☉ and ♂, who in Womens Nativities have most signification. Secondly, the seventh house and Lord thereof. Thirdly, the Planet or Planets in the seventh.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXXVII 'Of the Marriage of Women', p.600 [PDF p.634]

rule_en: Gender rule: in a woman's nativity the Sun takes the Moon's role and Mars takes Venus's role.
quote: we judge in the same manner as in Mens Nativities, accepting herein the ☉ in the place of ☽, and ♂ in the place of ♀
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXXVII 'Of the Marriage of Women', p.600 [PDF p.634]

rule_en: Whether she marries: significator fruitful, strong, in fortunate houses and well aspected by the fortunes promises marriage; barren, in unfortunate houses, weak and afflicted argues none. Venus occidental in the 7th and Saturn in the 4th: little desire to marry. Sun and Moon in masculine signs or the same masculine quarter: a virago, a refractory wife.
quote: If the Significator in a VVomans Nativity be fruitfull, strong in fortunate Houses, and in good aspect of the Fortunes, they then promise Marriage
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXXVII 'Of the Marriage of Women', p.600 [PDF p.634]

rule_en: When: the special time by direction of the Mid-heaven or the Sun; the general time by the Sun's quadrant: oriental quadrants marry in youth; occidental quarter, late and to an old man.
quote: The speciall time is discerned by direction of Mid-heaven or ☉; the generall time by the ☉
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXXVII 'Of the Marriage of Women', p.601 [PDF p.635]

rule_en: How many husbands: Sun in a sign of one form or aspecting one matutine planet, once; in a sign of many shapes or aspecting many matutine planets, more than once. 7th sign, its lord and Sun in a common sign, two husbands; Sun or Mars in a double-bodied sign, two; Venus and her dispositor in common or tropical signs, more. Also count planets conjoined to the Sun in his sign (partile or platick), else planets with dignity in the Sun's sign which the Sun applies to.
quote: ☉ in a Signe of one forme, or in aspect with one matutine Planet, notes she shall marry but once: ☉ in a Signe of many shapes, or in aspect unto many matutine Planets
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXXVII 'Of the Marriage of Women', p.601 [PDF p.635]

rule_en: Husband's description: sign of the 7th for his body, its lord for his conditions, with the aspects the Lord of the 7th and the Sun receive. A peregrine significator, or the Part of Fortune in the 3rd, means a stranger.
quote: Take the Signe of the seventh to signifie the shape of his Body, the Lord thereof his Conditions, with reference to the aspects the Lord of the seventh and ☉ have to the other Planets
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXXVII 'Of the Marriage of Women', p.601 [PDF p.635]; ends p.602

rule_en: Husband's wealth (Lilly's own way, against the Ancients): judge the 8th house, its lord and planets in it; strong and free from malefic aspects = rich husband. Lord of the 8th in his own house and angular: no fear for the husband's estate. Concord: significators in mutual reception or ⚹/△ or good aspects to fortunes = unity; contrary aspects, significators in 12th, 6th or 8th = no concord.
quote: Contrary to the rules of the Ancients, I constantly observe this way; To examine the strength of the eighth house, the Lord thereof, and Planet or Planets posited therein
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXXVII 'Of the Marriage of Women', p.602 [PDF p.636]

rule_en: Honour significators: (1) the luminaries, the Sun most, and planets beholding the lights within the moiety of their orbs, especially the Sun; (2) the Lord of the Mid-heaven; (3) planets in the Mid-heaven; (4) royal fixed stars of 1st or 2nd magnitude near the cusps of the 10th or 1st.
quote: Honour, Preferment, Dignity and Estimation is principally required from the Luminaries, wherein the ☉ is most considerable; and from the Planets which within the mediety of their Orbes doe behold the Lights
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'The tenth House, and the Judgments thereunto appertaining. Of the Honours or Dignities of the Native', p.615 [PDF p.649]

rule_en: Whether preferment: significators in house, exaltation or mutual reception of essential dignity give honours and public office; in triplicity, terms or face, mediocrity; peregrine or in detriment or fall without reception, small or none. In angles ample preferment; succedent moderate; 8th or cadent very little.
quote: These Significators if they be in their proper House, Exaltation, or in mutuall reception of essentiall Dignity, do bestow on the Native (who by birth may be capable thereof) Honours, Offices of publick trust
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIIII 'Whether the Native shall have Dignity or Preferments, or None at all', p.615 [PDF p.649]

rule_en: Angularity of the honour significators: angles ample, succedent moderate, 8th or cadent houses little.
quote: If they, viz. the Significators, are posited in angles, they give ample Preferment; in succedant, moderate Esteem, or little Honour or Dignity.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIIII, p.615 [PDF p.649]

rule_en: Significators within 5 degrees of royal fixed stars of 1st/2nd magnitude near the ecliptic show admirable preferment; such a conjunction counts three testimonies. Stars listed: Oculus ♉ 4°30′ ♊, Hercules 18°0′ ♋, Cor Leonis 24°30′ ♌, Spica 18°30′ ♎, Lucida Lancis 9°45′ ♏, Cor Scorpii 4°30′ ♐. Fortunes in the 10th promise preferment; malefics deny; mean planets a moderate state. Lord of the 1st in the 10th or Lord of the 10th in the 1st: good fame.
quote: In collecting the Testimonies of Honour, the Judicious allow for such a ☌ three testimonies.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIIII, p.616 [PDF p.650]

rule_en: Special rules of the luminaries: the luminary of the time (☉ by day, ☽ by night) exalted and in the MC with a regal ascendant and the lord of that light's sign in the ascendant or MC: kingly preferment (or authority 'in kind' for the lesser born). Luminaries cadent with the planets also cadent: wretched, vulgar life; neither light angular nor in a masculine sign, without benefics: abject people.
quote: The Luminary of the time being ☉ in a diurnall Geniture, ☽ in a nocturnall, in Exaltation and in the mid-heaven, the Signe ascending being also Regall
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'Speciall Rules of the two Luminaries', p.617 [PDF p.651]

rule_en: Lilly's caution: no positive judgment from a single aphorism; equal directions bring honour according to the native's capacity (a beggar's child versus a king's).
quote: for a Beggar's child may have a Nativity equall with a King's, but then they are not both the Sons of Kings
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIIII, p.616 [PDF p.650]

rule_en: The forcible aspects are only sextile, square (quadrate), trine and opposition; the conjunction is called an aspect 'very improperly'.
quote: The most forcible or strongest Rayes, Configurations or Aspects, are onely these (nominated before) the Sextil ⚹, Quadrate □, Trine △, Opposition ☍, we use to call the Conjunction ☌, an Aspect, but very improperly.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.105 [PDF p.139]

rule_en: Sextile: distance of a sixth of the circle (60 degrees); also called sexangular or hexagon. With the trine an argument of love, unity and friendship.
quote: A Sextil aspect is the distance of one Planet from another by the sixt part of the Zodiack or Circle; for six times sixty degr. doe make 360. degr.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.105 [PDF p.139]

rule_en: Square (quadrate, quadrangular, tetragonal): a fourth of the circle (90 degrees); a sign of imperfect enmity (reconciliation still possible).
quote: A Quadrate aspect, or Quadrangular, or Tetragonall, is the distance of two Points, or two Planets by a fourth part of the Circle
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.105 [PDF p.139]

rule_en: Trine (triangular, trigonal): 120 degrees, a third of the circle; argument of love and friendship and more forcible than the sextile.
quote: The Trine aspect consists of 120 degrees, or by a third part of the Circle
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.106 [PDF p.140]

rule_en: Opposition (diametral radiation): 180 degrees; argument of perfect hatred.
quote: An Opposition or Diametrall Radiation is, when two Planets are equally distant 180 degrees, or halfe the Circle from each other.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.106 [PDF p.140]

rule_en: Conjunction (coition, synod, congress): two planets in the same degree and minute of a sign; good or bad according as the planets are friends or enemies.
quote: A Conjunction, Coition, Synod or Congresse (for some use all these words) is, when two Planets are in one and the same degree and minute of a Signe
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.106 [PDF p.140]

rule_en: Good/evil: square = imperfect enmity; opposition = perfect hatred; sextile and trine = love, unity, friendship (trine stronger); conjunction good or bad by the planets' natures.
quote: the Quadrate Aspect is a signe of imperfect emnity; and that the Opposition is an aspect or argument of perfect hatred
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.106 [PDF p.140]

rule_en: Sextile and trine are benefic: arguments of love, unity and friendship, the trine more forcible.
quote: The Sextill and Trine aspects are arguments of Love, Unity and Friendship; but the △ is more forcible
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.106 [PDF p.140]

rule_en: Conjunctions are good or bad depending on whether the conjoined planets are friends or enemies.
quote: Conjunctions are good or bad, as the Planets in ☌ are friends or enemies to one another.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.106 [PDF p.140]

rule_en: Partile aspect: the planets exactly so many degrees apart as make the perfect aspect (e.g. ♀ 9 ♈ and ♃ 9 ♌ partile trine); a strong argument of performance, or of present evil when mischief is threatened.
quote: Partill aspect is when two Planets are exactly so many degrees from each other as make a perfect aspect
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.106 [PDF p.140]; continues p.107

rule_en: Platick aspect: within the moieties of both planets' orbs, not exact (e.g. ♀ 10 ♉, ♄ 18 ♍: platick trine, since the moieties 5 + 4 exceed the 8-degree distance).
quote: A Platick Aspect is that which admits of the Orbs or Rayes of two Planets that signifie any matter
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIX 'Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art, Accidents, and other materiall things happening amongst the Planets', p.107 [PDF p.141]

rule_en: Whether any profession at all: if none of ♂ ♀ ☿ qualifies by the first or second rule (angular in own dignity; or ruler of the MC sign in essential dignity) but only by the third to fifth (aspect to ☽; rising before ☉), the native usually follows some ignoble trade negligently or lives without any art.
quote: if none of these three Planets shall signifie the quality of the Native's Profession, according to the first or second rule, but according to the third, fourth or fifth; such usually handle some ignoble Profession
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLVIII 'Of the Magistery, Exercitation or Profession of the Native', p.625 [PDF p.659]

rule_en: Ptolemy's rule as reported: the lord of profession is taken from the Sun (the planet rising next before the Sun in the morning) and from the MC (its lord or a planet therein, if it beholds the Moon); a planet doing both is master of the native's actions, else take the one doing either. Lilly says he gathered most from the 10th sign and the sign/house of the Lord of the 10th.
quote: Ptolomey his judgement was, that the Lord of ones Profession was to be taken two wayes; from the ☉, and from the Signe of the mid-heaven
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLVIII 'Of the Magistery, Exercitation or Profession of the Native', p.626 [PDF p.660]

rule_en: A single significator gives a profession of its own nature (Venerial, Mercurial, Martial); joined strongly with another significator the natures mix (☿ lord of profession in strong good aspect of ♂: the native follows ♂'s trade). Other planets augment or diminish: ♃ assists, ♄ does mischief, ☉ gives power with the magistrate, ☽ credit with the common people.
quote: ♃ he assists, ♄ doth mischiefe, ☉ gives power with the Magistrate, the ☽ gives credit with the Common people
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.626 [PDF p.660]

rule_en: Where Saturn strongly inclines the disposition of the art, the native will be a husbandman, sailor, porter or carrier, shepherd, sexton.
quote: where ♄ doth strongly incline to the disposition of the Art, it's a miracle if the Native prove not a Husbandman, a Saylor, a Porter or carrier of Burthens, a Shepheard, Sexton of a Church
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.626 [PDF p.660]

rule_en: ☿ lord of the profession: trades of the brain rather than body strength: letters, numbers, writing, learning, eloquence, arithmetic, astrology, philosophy, merchandise, poetry, engines. Makes grammarians, chief secretaries, arithmeticians, geometricians, philosophers, poets, merchants. Without a good aspect of ♃ the native profits nothing by his endeavours.
quote: He therfore maks Gramarians, chief Secretaries, Arithmaticians Geometritians, Phylosophers, Poets, men full of employment, given to Merchandizing and Traffique, men given to Discipline
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', 'Of Mercury when he is Lord of the Profession', p.627 [PDF p.661]

rule_en: ☿ joined with ♄ (⚹/△ best; □/☍ impedes speech): servile offices in other men's employ, or a living about churches (soliciting alms, church affairs).
quote: he makes such men performe servile Offices in other mens employments, or such as lead their miserable Life in or about Churches
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', '☿ his signification when joyned with others', p.627 [PDF p.661]

rule_en: ☿ with ♄ and the same aspect to ♂: husbandmen, sailors, shepherds, cowkeepers, curriers, botchers, tailors, stone-cutters, carvers, interpreters of dreams (also 'sorcerers, superstitious' persons).
quote: he makes Husbandmen, Saylors, Shepherds, or Cow-keepers, Curriers, Botchers, Taylors, Stone-cutters or Carvers, Interpreters of Dreames
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.627 [PDF p.661]

rule_en: ☿ in ☌ or aspect with ♃: excellent orators, just judges of causes, divines, lawyers, rhetoricians, judges, exchangers or bankers; friends of great persons.
quote: it makes the Natives Friends of great Persons, Divines, Lawyers, Rhetoricians, Judges, an Exchanger or Banker of Moneys
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.627 [PDF p.661]

rule_en: ☿ bodily joined with ☉, not retrograde or combust but cazimi or in his dignities: acquainted with magistrates; scribes, receivers or treasurers of money, overseers, officers of public accounts, counsellors, chief justices. If ♂ has testimony with ☉ and ☿ (and ♄ any aspect) he inclines to chemistry or clipping/coining money (omitted from trades).
quote: he makes Scribes, Receivers or Treasurers of Moneys, Overseers, or employed as Officers in taking publike Accompts for the King or Common-wealth; Councellours, chiefe Justices
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.627 [PDF p.661]; continues p.628

rule_en: ☿ with ☽ or in her good aspect: understanding and divination; ☽ applying to ☿ in ♉ ♑ ♋ divination; in ♍ or ♏ astrologers; in ♈ ♌ ♎ natural diviners without art; in ♐ or ♓ given to magic. ☿ with ♀ (☌ or ⚹): eloquence and variety of manners.
quote: if the application be in ♍ or ♏, he makes Astrologians, &c.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.628 [PDF p.662]

rule_en: ♀ alone designing the profession: pleasure, delight, delicacy, feasting; she is an enemy to learning. Makes apothecaries, druggists, grocers, perfumers, vintners, victuallers, painters, jewellers, tire-makers, wardrobe-keepers, musicians.
quote: When she alone designes the Magistery, she makes Apothecaries, Drugsters, Grocers, Perfumers, Vintners, Victuallers, Painters, Jewellers, Tire-makers, Wardrobe-keepers, Musitians, &c.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', 'Of Venus when she alone designes the Profession', p.628 [PDF p.662]

rule_en: ♀ with ♄: merchants trading in things of pleasure; if either ill affected, scoffers, jesters, sly knaves, alehouse-keepers, sham magicians, poor painters, pretenders to a trade.
quote: ♀ commixed with ♄, makes Merchants, or such as Trade in things or Commodities tending to Pleasure
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', '♀ mixed with others', p.628 [PDF p.662]

rule_en: ♀ with ♃: divines, physicians, mercers, linen-drapers, silk-men, seamsters, haberdashers of small wares; great preferment by women or religion. ♀ combust gives no art; cazimi great wealth; in ☉'s dignities more excellent artist, fame and profit.
quote: ♀ mixed in signification with ♃, makes Divines, Physitians, Mercers, Linnen-Drapers, Silk-men, Seamsters, Haberdashers of small Wares
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.628 [PDF p.662]; continues p.629

rule_en: ♂ alone: laborious, hard, manual professions needing bodily strength, exercised by fire (fire also if ☉ aspects him); in a nocturnal geniture warfare and honour by wars. Well constituted: soldiers, horsemen, captains, commanders, huntsmen. Meanly dignified: champions, copper- and iron-smiths, founders, engineers, iron-instrument makers, husbandmen, physicians, surgeons, stone-cutters, carpenters, architects. Weak: cooks, wood-cleavers, curriers, labourers (also pirates, thieves).
quote: Being well constituted he makes Souldiers, Horsmen, Captains, Commanders of Armies, Hunsmen, &c.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', 'Of Mars when he alone is Significator of Profession', p.629 [PDF p.663]

rule_en: ♂ with ♄ or afflicted by his □/☍: loses magistracy and military signification; ditchers, day-labourers, gardeners, crossbow-makers, fletchers, leather-dressers; in an abject place colliers, chimney-sweeps, fire-makers, charcoal burners, millers, night-farmers.
quote: From such a position you shall predict Ditchers or Day-laboures, Gardiners, Crosse-bow makers, Fletchers, Dressers of Leather
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', '♂ mixed with others', p.629 [PDF p.663]

rule_en: ♂ and ♃ well posited: complete courtiers, fortunate in commands of war; unhappy by aspect/position: herdsmen, bailiffs, caterers, door-keepers, sutlers, tobacco-shop keepers.
quote: ♂ and ♃ well posited, makes compleat Courtiers, fortunate in the Commands of Warre
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.629 [PDF p.663]

rule_en: ♂ with ☉: magistracy rather than a profession; in unhappy aspect, working goldsmiths, coiners/minters, gold-mine diggers.
quote: ♂ with the ☉, inclines to Magistracy rather then to a Profession
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.629 [PDF p.663]; continues p.630

rule_en: ♂ with ☽: butchers; with ♄ also ruling: hedgers, day-labourers, fishermen, watermen, brewers, dyers.
quote: ♂ with the ☽ makes Butchers
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.630 [PDF p.664]

rule_en: ☿ and ♀ commixed: ingenious, voluble pleasant tongue; musicians (esp. in a Venerial sign), poets, orators, dancing-masters, tumblers, painters, makers of complexion-water, wax-chandlers, limners, playwrights, writing-masters, schoolmasters. Beholding ♄: graver trades, women's clothes and ornaments. ♃ ♀ ☿ in 3rd/5th/11th: pedagogues, preachers, advocates; in the 9th lawyers or public administrators.
quote: they usually make Musitians, especially when they are in a Veneriall Signe, Poets, Orators, Dancing-Masters, Tumblers or Dancers upon Ropes, Painters, makers of Complexion-water
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', 'Of Mercury and Venus commixed', p.630 [PDF p.664]

rule_en: ☿ with ♂ well disposed: sharp conceptions; physicians, surgeons, armourers, statue- and image-makers, champions, alchemists, engravers, public notaries, surveyors, printers. Ill placed and ♄ associated: forgers, cheats, thieves (omitted). ♃ in place of ♄: counsellors, attorneys, advocates, civil lawyers.
quote: Men of piercing understandings, Physitians, Chirurgions, Armorers, makers of Statua's, Images, Champions; Alchimists, Gravers, many times publique Notaries, Surveyors, Printers of Bookes
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', 'Of Mercury with Mars', p.630 [PDF p.664]; continues p.631

rule_en: ♂ and ♀ significators of art: labour with pleasure; cooks, poulterers, excellent physicians, barbers, apothecaries, surgeons, gardeners, dyers. With ♄: sextons, poor priests attending the sick, grave-makers, epitaph-makers. With ♃: zealous religious teachers, not covetous. (♂ ♀ ill placed: a bawd, omitted.)
quote: from hence you may judge, Cookes, Poulterers, excellent Physitians; Barbers, Apothecaries, Chirurgions, Gardiners, Dyers, &c.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', 'Mars and Venus significators of Art', p.631 [PDF p.665]

notes: Criminal callings Lilly lists in this case are omitted from data.trades by request.

rule_en: Fortune/fame in the profession: from the strength of the significator (Lord of Magistery). Potent in essential dignities, free of partile malefic configurations, angular and oriental: famous workman, great estimation and public reputation. Weak, occidental or cadent, oppressed by infortunes: a botcher, contemptible, not thriving.
quote: if he be potent in Essentiall dignities, and not afflicted by the malevolent partill configuration of the Infortunes, and be also posited in the angles of the Figure, and Orientall
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', 'With what successe', p.631 [PDF p.665]; continues p.632

rule_en: ♄ afflicting the significator: sluggard, lazy, fearful; ♂ impediting: rash, obstinate, conceited, infamous; both infortunes: numberless afflictions in the profession.
quote: when ♄ doth afflict the Significator, the Native proves a Sluggard, a Lazy Fellow, fearfull to put himselfe forward.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.632 [PDF p.666]

rule_en: Nature of the significators' signs: movable (♈♋♎♑) arts of wit (geometry, physic, astrology); fixed require learning or education (except ♏); human (♊♍♎♒) liberal arts taught with authority; watery and earthy (♋♏♓♉♑) water and earth trades (meadows, herbs, medicine, ships, fish, funerals); four-footed (♈♌♐) mechanical trades. Albubater: fiery signs fire trades (smithery, goldsmithery, baking, glass-making); earthy, earthy occupations.
quote: Movable Signes, as ♈ ♋ ♎ ♑, conduce to such Arts or professions as require a witty capacity
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLIX 'Severall experimented Aphorismes concerning the Native's Magistery, Trade or Profession', p.632 [PDF p.666]; continues p.633 (not extracted)

rule_en: Part of Fortune = Ascendant + Moon − Sun (subtract the Sun's place from the Moon's, adding 12 signs to the Moon if needed; add the remainder to the Ascendant; cast away 12 signs if over). Worked example: ☽ 21°18′ ♍, ☉ 4°18′ ♈, Asc 23°27′ ♌ gives ⊗ 10°27′ ♒.
quote: Thirdly, substract the place of the ☉ from the ☽, by adding twelve Signes to the ☽ if you cannot doe it otherwayes; what remaines, reserve and adde to the Signe and degree of the Ascendant
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I (opening of Book II), Chap. XXIII 'Of the Part of Fortune, and how to take it, either by Day or Night', p.143 [PDF p.177]; example ends p.144
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Same formula by day and by night: the heading says 'either night or day'. Lilly notes some reverse it at night (Sun − Moon + Asc) but follows Ptolemy, with whom 'al Practicioners' agree, using the day formula always.
quote: Some have used to take ⊗ in the night from the [☽] to the ☉; which if you doe, you must then make the place of the ☉ your first place
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I (opening of Book II), Chap. XXIII 'Of the Part of Fortune, and how to take it, either by Day or Night', p.144 [PDF p.178]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Next sentence on p.144: Ptolomie, day and night takes it as above directed, with whom al Practicioners at this day consent. The bracketed [☽] is an editorial fill: in the image the glyph in 'from the ☽ to the ☉' is a blank rule; read from context.

rule_en: Lilly's rule of thumb: whether by day or night, the Part of Fortune is as far from the Ascendant as the Moon is from the Sun (new Moon: in the Ascendant; first quarter 4th house; full 7th; last quarter 10th).
quote: Whether your Figure be by day or night, observe this Method; for how many degrees the ☉ is distant from the ☽, so many is the ⊗ from the Ascendant
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I (opening of Book II), Chap. XXIII 'Of the Part of Fortune, and how to take it, either by Day or Night', p.144 [PDF p.178]

rule_en: Use: ⊗ has no aspect of its own but receives aspects; well placed (good house, angle, good aspect of a benefic) the querent's estate is sound and firm.
quote: it hath no aspect, but any Planets may cast their aspect unto it.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I (opening of Book II), Chap. XXIII 'Of the Part of Fortune, and how to take it, either by Day or Night', p.143 [PDF p.177]
