notes: Chapter is numbered XXIII in this copy (contents list it at p.143). Book III p.552 uses ⊗ and its lord as significators of wealth but does not restate the formula (not separately checked).

rule_en: Brethren and sisters: best judged from the nativity of the first-born. Significators: (1) the 3rd house from 5° before its cusp to 5° before the next; (2) the Lord of the 3rd and planets intercepted there; (3) ♂ general significator of brethren, ☽ of sisters. Mostly fruitful planets in prolific signs = many; barren in barren signs = few or none; mixed = few.
quote: Thirdly, ♂ who is ever a generall Significator of Brethren, but the ☽ of Sisters.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXVIII 'If have Brethren or Sisters', p.565 [PDF p.599]; chapter begins p.564
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Fruitful planets ♃ ♀ (some add ☊); barren ♄ ♂ and ☋; luminaries mediocre (☉ nearer barren, ☽ more fruitful); ☿ indifferent, takes the nature of the planet he is configured with. Aspect strength order: ☌ > △ > ⚹ > □ > ☍; partile before platick.
quote: We call the Fruitfull or Prolificall Planets, ♃ ♀; and some do adde hereunto ☊, being of the nature of ♃ and ♀.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXVIII, p.565 [PDF p.599]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Lilly then lists each sign's fruitfulness for brethren (♈ rather barren, ♉ fruitful, ♊ barren...) from p.565; not extracted beyond ♊.

rule_en: Three questions for the 3rd house: whether the native has brothers or sisters; their condition; whether they live in unity and concord.
quote: first, I declare Whether the Native shall have Brothers or Sisters: Secondly, What shall their condition be: Thirdly, Whether the Native and they shall live in unity and concord
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'Judgments upon the third House. Of Kinred, viz. Brethren and Sisters', p.564 [PDF p.598]

rule_en: Father: significators are (1) the 4th house, (2) its Lord, (3) ☉ in a diurnal geniture, ♄ in a nocturnal, (4) planets in the 4th. Mostly strong and fortunate, in good aspect of ♃ or ♀: happy condition of the father after the birth; afflicted: low condition. Best judged from the father's own nativity. Lord of 4th in reception or △/⚹ with Lord of the ascendant: flourishing father. ☉ or ♃ in the 4th: father of good quality.
quote: The Significators of the Father in every Geniture are: First, the fourth house; secondly, the Lord thereof: thirdly, the ☉ in a diurnall Geniture, ♄ in a nocturnall: fourthly, the Planet or Planets in the fourth
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'Judgments upon the fourth House. Concerning Parents, &c. And Patrimony of the Father', p.569 [PDF p.603]

notes: Lilly's father-longevity lines (p.570) intentionally not extracted.

rule_en: Mother (Chap. CXXII): significators are (1) the 10th house, (2) its Lord, (3) ♀ in a diurnal nativity, ☽ in a nocturnal, (4) planets in the 10th. Well constituted (good houses, essentially dignified) = good to the mother; ☽ much afflicted = misery or sickness to her.
quote: The Mothers Significators are, first, the tenth house; secondly, the Lord thereof; thirdly, ♀ in a diurnall Nativity, ☽ in a nocturnall; fourthly, a Planet or Planets in the tenth house.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXII 'Of the Mother', p.570 [PDF p.604]

rule_en: ☉ better dignified than ☽: father better descended than the mother, and vice versa.
quote: ☉ better dignified then the ☽, shew the Father better descended then the Mother; and so the the contrary.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'Judgments upon the fourth House', p.570 [PDF p.604]

notes: 'the the' as printed.

rule_en: Inheritance (Chap. CXXIIII): ☉ joined to ♃ or ♀ by day (♄ and ☽ to the same by night), or in good aspect with them, especially in the 2nd or 4th, or ruling the 4th: a good patrimony which the native improves. ♂ afflicting ☉ by day or ♄ by night without benefic help: the native dissipates his father's estate.
quote: The ☉ conjoyned to ♃ or ♀ by day, or ♄ and ☽ to the same Planets in a nocturnall Nativity, or in good aspect with them, especially in the second or fourth
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXXIIII 'Whether the Native will enjoy the Estate of his Father; and whether he shall waste or consume it', p.572 [PDF p.606]; continues p.573
